title: Proactive warmup & backpressure simulation: SLO instrumentation and multi-region failover dashboard
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Runbook and dashboard work to instrument proactive service warmup behavior and a backpressure simulation harness so we can validate SLOs (token-latency and request success) during multi-region failover and scaled admission events. Focus is on measurable golden signals across three phases: warmup, steady-state, and overload, with a console-facing dashboard and automated synthetic scenarios to reproduce incidents without hitting production traffic.

Goals:
- Add sequence-windowed token-latency SLIs (p50/p95/p99) with warmup tags so we can differentiate cold-start/warmup tail behavior from steady-state.
- Create a deterministic backpressure simulation harness that can inject admission pressure across regions and measure how circuit breakers/fanout routing react.
- Deliver a Grafana/Console dashboard combining golden signals, warmup cohort breakdown, admission rate curves, and regional failover timelines.
- Define acceptance criteria and an automated test suite that runs in CI to validate rollout safety for admission/hysteresis changes.

Why this work matters:
We observed two incidents where model containers scaled up and regional traffic redirected, producing elevated p99 token latency for 10-30 minutes as caches and KV layers warmed. Current SLO tooling conflates cold-start noise with steady-state regressions, complicating incident postmortems and rollback decisions. By instrumenting warmup as a first-class signal and coupling it with a synthetic backpressure simulator, we can both prevent surprising SLO violations and safely tune admission/circuit policies.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope includes telemetry metrics, SLI tagging schema, simulation harness, dashboard panels, and CI smoke tests.
- Non-goal: deeper runtime kernel changes or model quantization tuning (those are separate tickets).

Design notes and decisions so far:
- We will derive warmup cohorts by a small state machine on the serving node: first request window (0-30s), warmup window (30s-5m), warm (5m+). These windows are configurable by runtime flags.
- Token-latency SLIs will be emitted both per-request and per-token-windowed (sliding 50-token window) to capture decode amplification during cold caches.
- Backpressure simulator will use synthetic clients that can drive admission policies (burst, sustained, and ramp) and toggle fanout routing to secondary regions to validate failover behaviors.
- Dashboard will implement an explicit 'Warmup Mode' time striping so operators can toggle view to include/exclude warmup cohorts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard contains panels for: golden signals (error-rate, p95/p99 token latency), warmup cohort split, regional failover timeline, admission score histogram, and simulated scenario playback.
- CI smoke tests run the backpressure simulator against staging and assert no increase in production-flag metrics beyond thresholds when run against feature-flagged nodes.
- SLI definitions updated in SLO registry and reflected in alerting rules with warmup-aware suppression for the first 5 minutes after a scale event.
- Playbook section added to Console runbook for interpreting warmup vs steady-state SLO breaches.

Work breakdown (high level):
- Instrumentation (backend): emit warmup-tagged token latency metrics, admission-score export, and region-routing events.
- Simulation harness: implement traffic generator, orchestration scripts to create admission profiles, and recorder to produce timeline artifacts.
- Dashboard: create Grafana panels + Console embedding, scenario playback UI for simulated events.
- CI/tests: add integration test that runs a smoke simulation and validates metric invariants.
- Documentation & runbook: Confluence doc + on-call playbook additions.

Artifacts / Links:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/WARMUP-BACKPRESSURE-SIM (internal)
- Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/214
- Prototype Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Sim/WarmupBackpressure (staging)

test_plan: 1) Unit tests for warmup tag logic and metric emission. 2) Integration: run simulator in staging (3 Node) and assert that warmup cohort p99 >> steady-state but global SLO remains within threshold with admission policies enabled. 3) Regression CI: ensure dashboard panels render and playback scenario artifacts. 4) Chaos test: simulate region loss and ensure automatic fanout fallback happens within configured SLA.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1: Merge metric emission behind feature flag and run simulator in staging for 2 weeks.
- Phase 2: Enable in canary subset of runtime nodes and validate metrics.
- Phase 3: Release dashboard to Console read-only for SREs and PMs.
- Phase 4: Full rollout with playbook and alerting changes; monitor for 72h before adjusting thresholds.
monitoring_playbook:
- If p99 token-latency warms beyond X ms during warmup window, mark as warmup and do not trigger pager.
- If warmup-duration exceeds expected window (configurable), escalate to SRE to check KV miss rates and container cold-start patterns.
- For simulation runs, mark all related traces with tag simulated=true and suppress production alerts.
- Provide quick links in dashboard to open GitHub PRs and the incident runbook.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: 1) Fine-grained warmup windows give better signal but add complexity to metrics ingestion and storage. We will roll out with coarse windows first and iterate. 2) Simulator fidelity vs test safety: we will prefer deterministic admission feeders that avoid saturating shared infra by default.
Known risks: false positives if downstream layers change their warmup behavior (e.g., kernel or KV changes). Mitigation: add a daily synthetic job to baseline warmup curves.
